tutorials.title: Ask the assistant and review changes

steps.label: Click the Assistant button
Type a question
Click Send
The answer comes from your project. See sources shows what it used
Sources list the scenes and steps behind the answer
In the Screenplay, click the Assistant button
Ask for a change and click Send
Review the Proposed Changes. Nothing is added until you apply
Applied as one step you can undo

tutorials.title: Set up the offline AI assistant

steps.label: Click the Assistant button in the top bar
Open the ... menu of the AI Assistant
Choose Offline AI settings…
AI Ready. Technical details lists the engine and models
Everything runs on this computer

tutorials.title: Restore a backup or project package

steps.label: On the projects screen

steps.target: [title="Restore a backup or open a project package"]
steps.label: Click Restore Backup or Package…
Click Choose Package… and pick the .ofbackup or .ofproject file

tutorials.title: Tag a prop in a scene breakdown

steps.label: In the scene list, click Scene 5

steps.target: text=A long corridor with green walls
steps.label: Select the words to tag in the script
Choose a category, here Props
Type the item name; an existing catalog item is offered
Click Add to Scene 5
The prop is tagged in Scene 5 and linked to the catalog

tutorials.title: Add a line to the budget

steps.label: Click Add Line
Type the line item, choose a category and enter the planned amount
Click Add Line
The line is added and the planned total updates

tutorials.title: Create a call sheet from a shooting day

steps.label: Click Create Call Sheet
Choose the shooting day, here Shoot Day 4
Click Create Call Sheet
The draft opens filled from the schedule; click Add Section
Add weather, crew, walkie channels, notes and more, then Finalize and Export PDF

tutorials.title: Assign an actor to a character

steps.label: Click Assign next to a character that needs casting
Type the actor's name and choose the character they play
Pick Primary actor or Alternate / double, then click Assign

tutorials.title: Add and edit characters

steps.label: In Story, open the Characters tab
Click Add Character
Type a name
OpenFrame warns about a possible match. Cancel and use the existing character
Click Edit to fill in the details
Name, role and short description, saved with Save

tutorials.title: Create your first project

steps.label: Click Create Project
Type a title and choose Feature Film or Short Film
Optional details are there if you want them
Click Create
The new project opens on its Home page

tutorials.title: Compare drafts, lock and revise

steps.label: Click Compare to see what changed between two drafts
Changes are listed and marked side by side. Back to script
When the script is ready to shoot, click Lock
Check the details and click Lock as Shooting Draft
Start typing in the locked draft
OpenFrame offers a revision instead. Click Start Revision
Pick a colour and add a reason if you like
Click Start Revision
You now write in Revision A; the locked draft never changes

tutorials.title: Export a script and preview the pages

steps.label: Click Export in the screenplay toolbar
Pick a format: PDF, Final Draft (.fdx), Fountain, DOCX. Additional formats… shows more
Choose Entire draft or Selected scenes
Tick the scenes you want
Click Preview… to check the pages
Print or Export PDF from the preview; Export… saves the chosen format

tutorials.title: Organise project files in a folder

steps.label: In the left rail, open Files
Click New Folder
Type a folder name
Click Create
The new folder opens, ready for files

tutorials.title: Start OpenFrame Studio for the first time

steps.label: OpenFrame asks what to call you. Clear the suggested name
Type your name, then click Continue
Application Home opens, ready for your first project

tutorials.title: Collect ideas in the Idea Vault

steps.label: Click Add to choose what to collect
Pick Quick Capture for a fast idea
Type the idea
Click Save (or press Enter)
Organise: click New Collection in the side panel
Name the collection and click Create
The collection is ready in the side panel

tutorials.title: Import an existing script

steps.label: Click + (Create)
Choose Import Screenplay…
Choose a file with Browse…, paste text, or open a sample script
Click Preview
Check scenes, characters and warnings, then click Import
Import complete. Nothing else in your project was changed

tutorials.title: Keep scouting notes on a location

steps.label: Right-click a location card
Choose Open
Scroll down to the practical notes
Fill in parking, noise, permission, access, power and other notes

tutorials.title: Pin, archive and restore projects

steps.label: Pinned projects sit at the top. Click the ... button on a card
The menu has Rename, Duplicate Project, Pin or Unpin, Archive. Click Archive
Archived, not deleted. Click Open Archived
Click Restore to bring it back
The project is back in your projects

tutorials.title: Make a moodboard for your film

steps.label: In Production, open the Moodboards tab
Click New Moodboard
Pick a suggested name, or type your own board name
Click Create Moodboard
The new board opens, empty, ready for images, notes and links

tutorials.title: Project notes and templates

steps.target: button[aria-label="Project: Night Bus. Switch or manage projects"]
steps.label: Open the project menu
Choose Notes & Tasks
Click New Note
Give it a title and write the note
The note saves as you type and joins the list
Built-in templates are listed. Click Create Template
Name it, pick a type and where to keep it
Click Create
Your template joins the list

tutorials.title: Find your way around a project

steps.target: button[aria-label="Project: Night Bus. Switch or manage projects"]
steps.label: The project name at the top opens the project menu
The + button creates anything: ideas, acts, scene cards, characters and more
Search the whole project from the top bar (Ctrl+K)
Type a name or word
Results from every section, each labelled with its type

tutorials.title: Undo a delete and use Recently Deleted

steps.label: Here a short note is written first
Click Delete
It moves to Recently Deleted; click Undo in the message to bring it back

tutorials.title: Save a report snapshot and export it

steps.label: On a report, click Save snapshot
Click Back to live reports
Click Export
Pick PDF, CSV or Excel (XLSX) and click Export…

tutorials.title: Create a shooting day

steps.label: In Production, open the Schedule tab
Click Create Shooting Day
Pick the shooting date and type day notes
Click Create Day
Shoot Day 4 is added to the stripboard; click it
The day opens, ready for scenes, breaks and times

tutorials.title: Comments and private scene notes

steps.label: Select some words in the script
Click the Comment button that appears
Write the comment in the Comments panel and click Comment
Open View and more
Choose Writing Room Mode
Panels open as tabs on the right. Close Beat Board
Open Scene Notes
Click Add private note and type
Only you see private notes. Click Save

tutorials.title: Tour the project settings

steps.label: Click Settings (the gear at the top right)
Project settings hold the title, type and status; open Writing
Spelling and your dictionary are here; open Keyboard shortcuts
Change any shortcut; open Offline AI
Check the offline AI; open Advanced
Breakdown category colours are here; open Appearance
Choose the mode and theme

tutorials.title: Open a shot and set its details

steps.label: In Production, open the Shot Lists tab

steps.target: button[aria-label="Open shot 1A: Wide: the bus arrives at the empty stand"]
steps.label: Right-click shot 1A
Choose Open
Set the shot size, movement, angle and lens in the shot details

tutorials.title: Prepare sides for one actor

steps.label: From the Daily View, open the Sides tab
Choose the shooting day, here Shoot Day 4
Under For, choose Selected cast
Tick the actor who needs sides
The preview shows that actor's pages; Save Sides or Export PDF

tutorials.title: Plan your story on the Beat Board

steps.label: In Story, open the Board tab
Acts are columns, sequences group scene cards, beats mark turns. Add creates any of them
Press Esc to close the menu

steps.target: div[aria-label="Scene Card: Lakshmi steps off the night bus"]
steps.label: Right-click a scene card
Click Open
The card opens: scene heading, short and long description, notes

tutorials.title: Draw a storyboard panel

steps.label: In Production, open the Storyboards tab
Click Add Panel
Choose Draw / Sketch
Sketch the frame with the pen
Click Save Panel to add the sketch as a new panel

tutorials.title: Add a task linked to a scene or item

steps.label: In the project menu, choose Notes & Tasks
Click New Task
Type the task, set a due date and add notes

steps.target: input[aria-label="Find a scene, location, character, shooting day or call sheet"]
steps.label: Under Related to, search for what the task is about
Pick the related item
Click Add Task
The task joins the open tasks with its link and due date

tutorials.title: Choose Light, Dark and a theme

steps.target: button[aria-label="Project: Night Bus. Switch or manage projects"]
steps.label: Open the project menu
Choose Appearance
Under Mode choose Light, Dark or System, then pick a theme

tutorials.title: Write in the screenplay editor

steps.label: Click Continue screenplay

steps.target: button[aria-label="Element type: Scene Heading. Change element type"]
steps.label: The bar at the bottom shows the element type of the line you are in. Click it
Pick a type or use Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+7. Press Esc to close
On a character line, start typing a name
OpenFrame suggests characters already in the script. Enter accepts

tutorials.reason: The assistant is part of the Mac app, but this Mac walkthrough is not ready yet. The steps match the Windows tutorial.
The assistant is part of the Mac app, but this Mac walkthrough is not ready yet. The steps match the Windows tutorial.

tutorials.title: Back up a project and restore it

steps.label: With the project open, choose File > Back Up Project…
Type an optional label. Use Browse… to choose where to save, ideally another disk
Click Create Backup
Backup created. Show in folder reveals the .ofbackup file
Choose File > Restore Backup or Package…
Click Choose Package… and pick the .ofbackup or .ofproject file
The project already exists here, so keep Open as Copy and click Open as Copy
The backup opens as Night Bus (copy). The original project is untouched

tutorials.title: Tag a script element in the breakdown

steps.label: In Breakdown, scene 1 is open. Select the words to tag in the script (here REGISTER)
Click Tag Selection
Check the Category (Props) and the Name, then click Add to Scene 1
Register appears under Props in the Scene 1 breakdown and is added to the production catalog

tutorials.title: Start a simple budget

steps.label: In Production, Budget, pick a currency and click Start Budget
Click Add Line
Choose a category, type the line item, the planned amount and, once spent, the actual amount
Click Add Line
Lines group by category with totals, and Planned, Actual and Difference sit at the top

tutorials.title: Make a call sheet for a shooting day

steps.label: In Call Sheets, click Create Call Sheet
Pick the shooting day and template, then click Create Call Sheet
The call sheet fills in from the schedule. Type call times and contacts in the fields, then click Add Section
Choose Weather
Click Export PDF
The Export Call Sheet sheet creates the PDF snapshot to send. Click Export… and choose where to save

tutorials.title: Cast actors and add crew

steps.label: In Production, Cast & Crew, Cast, click Assign next to KIRAN
Type the actor name
Keep Primary actor and click Assign
Meera Iyer now plays KIRAN. DEVI still needs casting
In Production, Cast & Crew, switch to Crew and click Add Person. Type the name and the role
Pick a Department and add contact details if you like, then click Add to Crew
The crew member opens in the inspector with Role, Department, Contact and availability

tutorials.title: Add a character

steps.label: In Story, click Characters
Click Add Character
Type a name, and if you like a role and a short description
Click Create Character
The character page lists every scene the character appears in

tutorials.title: Create your first project

steps.label: Click Create Project
Type a title for the film
Click Create
The new project opens on its Project Home

tutorials.title: Start a new draft and compare it

steps.label: Click the Draft menu at the bottom of the page
Choose New Draft…
Name the draft
Click Create Draft
Rewrite a few lines in the new draft
Click Compare
Both drafts side by side, with every change listed

tutorials.title: Export your screenplay

steps.label: Click Screenplay Tools
Choose Import and Export, then Export Screenplay…
Choose a format, here Final Draft (.fdx)
Check the options, then click Export… and choose where to save

tutorials.title: Add a file to the project

steps.label: In Files, click Add File
Choose Copy into project… and pick the file in the Open panel
The file is listed as stored in the project, with Open and a More actions menu

tutorials.title: Start OpenFrame Studio for the first time

steps.target: a[aria-label="Your name: Welcome, a name typed"]
steps.label: Type the name you want on your notes and tasks
Click Continue
Application Home opens, ready for your first project

tutorials.title: Capture an idea in the Idea Vault

steps.label: Click Quick Capture, or press Shift+Cmd+N
Type the idea
Click Save, or press Return
The idea is saved as a card in the Project Idea Vault

tutorials.title: Bring in an existing screenplay

steps.label: Click Screenplay Tools
Choose Import and Export, then Import Screenplay…
Choose a file with Browse…, paste text, or open a sample, then click Preview

tutorials.title: Add a location and set its status

steps.label: In Production, Locations, click Add Location. Type the name, and the address and nearest hospital if you know them
Click Add Location
The location opens in the inspector. Set its status to Confirmed
The card now reads Confirmed. Photos, contact and safety details live in the same inspector

tutorials.title: Pin, archive and restore projects

steps.label: Open Actions for Night Bus and choose Pin
Open Actions for Empty Short and choose Archive
Click Open Archived
Click Restore
The project is back in your projects

tutorials.title: Build a moodboard for the film

steps.label: In Production, Moodboards, click New Moodboard. In the sheet, click the suggestion Overall Look
Click Create Moodboard
The empty board opens. Click Add Note
Type the note
Click Add Note
Notes and links sit on the canvas. Select a tile to edit it
The item opens in the inspector, with its note, the internal note switch and a caption

tutorials.title: Preview a built-in template

steps.label: In Project Settings, click Templates
Open Actions for Feature Film Screenplay
Choose Preview
Preview the template, then use it in this project

tutorials.title: Find your way around a project

steps.label: Click Home in the sidebar
Click Search, or press Cmd+K
Type a name or a word from the script
Matching scenes and commands appear; pick one to jump there

tutorials.title: Restore a deleted item

steps.label: On Project Home, click Recently Deleted
Deleted items wait here for 30 days. Click Restore next to Old catering list
The note goes back to Notes & Tasks. The message offers Undo

tutorials.title: Read production reports

steps.label: In Production, Reports, the Scene Report shows. Click Location Report
Click Cast Scene Report
Click Prop Report
Each report is built live from the breakdown and the schedule. Use the filter, Save snapshot or Export

tutorials.title: Build a shooting schedule

steps.label: In Production, Schedule, click Create Shooting Schedule
Check the screenplay source and click Create Schedule
All 10 scenes start in Unscheduled. Click Create Shooting Day
Enter a shooting date (YYYY-MM-DD, optional) and click Create Day. Repeat for each day
Three days are on the board. Open the actions of the Scene 1 strip
Choose Move to and pick a shooting day, or drag the strip onto a day
The scenes sit in their days. Click the warnings button
Schedule assistance lists practical warnings, such as an actor needed at two locations, with Open affected item, Move scene and Keep anyway

tutorials.title: Comment on the script and reply

steps.label: Type your comment on the selected words, then click Comment
Click Reply under the comment
Type a reply and click Reply
The comment and its reply stay beside the script

tutorials.title: Tour the Settings window

steps.label: Click Settings (or choose OpenFrame Studio > Settings…, Cmd+,)
General holds your display name and the data folder. Click Appearance
Appearance holds Mode and Theme. Click Keyboard Shortcuts
Change, remove or add keys for 23 commands. Click Offline AI
Offline AI manages the on-device model. Click Diagnostics
Diagnostics helps when something needs support

tutorials.title: Plan shots in a shot list

steps.label: In Production, Shot Lists, open the Scene pop-up
Choose Scene 1
Type a short shot description, then click Add Shot. Repeat for each shot
Shots get letters 1A, 1B, 1C. Control-click (right-click) a shot
Choose Open
The shot opens in the inspector with its description, optional technical details, a reference image and storyboard links

tutorials.title: Save and export sides for a day

steps.label: In Production, Sides, Shoot Day 1 is chosen with its scenes. Tick Include call-sheet cover page
The preview adds the cover page. Click Save Sides
The sides are saved as a snapshot. Click the saved entry to open it
The saved sides open. Export PDF makes the file for the team

tutorials.title: Build a Beat Board

steps.label: Click Add
Choose Act
Name the act and press Return
Click Add Sequence in the act
Name the sequence and press Return
Click Add scene in the sequence
A new scene card waits for a short description

tutorials.title: Add storyboard panels to a scene

steps.label: In Production, Storyboards, with a scene chosen, click Add Panel
Choose Empty Panel. Repeat to add more panels
Control-click (right-click) a panel
The panel menu offers Open, Move Earlier, Move Later, Move to Storyboard…, Link Shot… and Delete

tutorials.title: Add a task with a due date

steps.label: In Notes & Tasks, click New Task
Type the task
Tick Set a due date and pick the date
Choose an owner from Owner if needed, then click Add Task
The task is in the Tasks list with its due date. Tick its box to mark it done

tutorials.title: Change the theme

steps.label: Click Settings (or choose OpenFrame Studio > Settings…, Cmd+,)
In the Settings window, click Appearance
Mode offers System, Light and Dark. Click a theme, here Black and White
The theme applies at once across the app

tutorials.title: Write your first scene

steps.label: Click Element to see the element types
Press Esc to close the menu
Start a scene heading
Finish the heading, press Return and write the action
Your first scene is on the page and in the scene list
